fullnameOverride.description: Override the fully qualified release name (the umbrella chart pins the Service name through this).

global.description: Platform-wide values an umbrella chart (agent-platform) shares with every component; Helm forwards them to this chart. `oauth.*` reads the identity contract as its defaults: `global.identity.issuerUrl`, `global.identity.clientId`, `global.identity.existingSecret`, `global.identity.ca.secretName` / `.key`, and `global.domain` for the OAuth base URL. Empty here; a standalone install sets `oauth.*` directly.

devices.description: The node's KVM devices, mounted into the pod from the node as hostPath character devices: /dev/kvm (hardware virtualization) and /dev/vhost-vsock (the guests' READY=1 and ssh). Off, the pod starts without them and GET /api/v1/host reports them under `missing` — for a cluster without KVM nodes, and for the chart's own install smoke.

tag.description: Image tag. Defaults to the chart appVersion.

existingClaim.description: The image directory `--image-dir` reads (README "Images"): the base image, its UKI and the Kubernetes sysext layers `make -C images` in a vm-manager checkout builds, with the policy.json that carries the golden PCR values. Mounted from an existing PersistentVolumeClaim an operator fills, or from a node path (a lab: agentlab mounts its checkout's images/build into the kind node); neither means an empty emptyDir and no bootable image. `vm-manager image golden` writes policy.json from outside the pod, so the mount is read-only by default.

path.description: MCP endpoint path (the REST API is always served).

enabled.description: Serve the Prometheus exposition at GET /metrics, outside the OAuth guard like /healthz.

guestSeriesLimit.description: Series kept per VM from one systemd-report upload.

auth.description: How muster authenticates to this server; rendered only with `oauth.enabled`. `forwardToken` makes muster forward the session's IdP id_token byte-identical. `requiredAudiences` are extra audiences that token must carry, trusted as bearer audiences by construction.

autoStart.description: Start the server connection when muster initializes.

enabled.description: Register this server with muster by rendering an `mcpservers.muster.giantswarm.io` CR in the release namespace. Tools then appear as `x_<name>_<tool>`. The CR carries `agent-platform.giantswarm.io/tool-group: agent-platform`: the platform's own management surface, next to agent-manager and model-manager.

labels.description: Extra labels on the MCPServer CR (merged last: they may override the tool-group label).

name.description: MCPServer CR name (drives the tool prefix).

enabled.description: Create a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy for the pod.

guestEgress.description: The guests' traffic leaves the pod: the networks are userspace NAT (gvisor-tap-vsock) and a VM reaches whatever the pod reaches, so the policy admits every egress destination. False limits egress to DNS and the identity provider — VMs then have no network beyond their own.

ingressNamespaces.description: Namespaces allowed to reach the API (label kubernetes.io/metadata.name). Empty allows ingress from the release namespace only.

nodeSelector.description: Node selector: the KVM node(s) — a label such as `kvm.giantswarm.io/enabled: "true"` on nodes that expose /dev/kvm.

allowPublicClientRegistration.description: Accept unauthenticated dynamic client registration (labs only).

baseURL.description: Public base URL of this server: the issuer of its own OAuth metadata (https, or http on loopback). Empty derives `https://<fullname>.<global.domain>` when `global.domain` is set.

allowPrivateURLs.description: Let the issuer resolve to a private or loopback address (an in-cluster Dex).

caSecret.description: Secret with the CA of a Dex that serves a private certificate; `global.identity.ca.secretName` / `global.identity.ca.key`.

clientID.description: Dex OAuth client ID. Empty falls back to `global.identity.clientId`.

issuerURL.description: Dex issuer URL. Empty falls back to `global.identity.issuerUrl`.

enabled.description: Make vm-manager an OAuth 2.1 resource server (mcp-oauth): the MCP endpoint and the REST API require a bearer token the platform identity provider issued, and every call carries the caller's identity. On the Agent Platform muster forwards the session's IdP id_token to this server (MCPServer `auth.forwardToken`, rendered below), validated against the IdP's JWKS when its audience is in `trustedAudiences`. Off: anonymous — only for a server nothing but a trusted proxy can reach.

existingSecret.description: Existing Secret with the provider credentials: `dex-client-secret` (dex) or `google-client-secret` (+ optional `google-client-id`) (google). Empty falls back to `global.identity.existingSecret`, whose `dex-client-secret` is the platform client's; without that, the chart renders a Secret from the values above.

clientID.description: Google OAuth client ID (not secret; may also come from the Secret key `google-client-id` when empty).

allowPrivateIPs.description: Let the IdP's JWKS endpoint resolve to a private address when validating forwarded tokens (an in-cluster Dex).

trustedAudiences.description: OAuth client IDs whose IdP id_tokens are accepted as bearer tokens (SSO token forwarding). Empty falls back to `[global.identity.clientId]`, the platform client MCP clients and the muster CLI log in with. The server trusts the union of this list and `muster.mcpServer.auth.requiredAudiences` (in that order, without duplicates).

existingClaim.description: Keep the state directory (VM records, disks, vTPM state, consoles) on a PersistentVolumeClaim: an existing claim's name, or `create: true` to render one from the settings below. With neither the state is an emptyDir and the VMs die with the pod — they end with the process anyway next `start_vm`.

podSecurityContext.description: Pod security context. Root: /dev/kvm is root:kvm on every node and the process forks QEMU and swtpm as its own children.

replicaCount.description: Number of replicas. One: the VMs are children of the one process and the state directory is its own. The Deployment rolls with Recreate for the same reason.

resources.description: Container resources. The VMs are QEMU processes inside this container, so a memory limit bounds the sum of their memory too; none by default.

securityContext.description: Container security context. Privileged, on purpose: a hostPath device mounted into an unprivileged container is denied by the device cgroup (open(2) fails with EPERM) unless a device plugin hands it out, so the privileged flag is what makes /dev/kvm and /dev/vhost-vsock usable. No capability is used beyond that (no bridges, no tap devices, no CAP_NET_ADMIN: the networks are userspace).

create.description: Create a ServiceAccount. vm-manager calls no Kubernetes API; the token is never mounted.

attestation.description: How guest TPM quotes are judged: `verify` (against the image policy and its golden values) or `noop`.

bootTimeout.description: `READY=1` ceiling, then `running`; raise it when user-data runs `kubeadm init` with image pulls.

defaultNetwork.description: Its name; `create_vm` attaches to it unless told otherwise.

learnGolden.description: Bring-up of a new image or firmware only: accept golden PCRs the image policy has no value for and record them for `vm-manager image golden`.

networkSubnet.description: CIDR of the default network, created at startup when missing.

code.description: OVMF firmware code image and variable store template; empty probes the known locations (the image ships Ubuntu's under /usr/share/OVMF).

stopTimeout.description: Graceful power-down before SIGKILL, also on shutdown.
